name: Zambia
summary_text: Zambia is dangerous for trans visitors. The Penal Code criminalises same-sex conduct (up to 14 years) with documented recent enforcement: Amnesty International's November 2024 campaign highlights Madalitso Zulu, serving a 15-year sentence with hard labour; Amnesty's 2024 regional report documents rising hostility in Zambia. There is no legal gender recognition, religious leaders lead anti-LGBT mobilisation, and police are perpetrators more than protectors. For a visitor: visible trans presentation risks arrest; the documented serving-sentence case shows courts impose maximum terms.

sources.title: Madalitso’s story: The persecution of LGBTI people in Zambia - Amnesty International
sources.claim_summary: Amnesty International campaign story (Nov 2024): 'Madalitso's story' - Madalitso Zulu, a 36-year-old health professional, is serving a 15-year prison sentence with hard labour simply for identifying as gay; profile of his medical career, Covid-19 contributions, and imprisonment.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust country profile documents Zambia's criminalisation of same-sex activity (up to 14 years).

sources.title: Africa: We are facing extinction: Escalating anti-LGBTI sentiment, the weaponization of law and their human rights implications in select African countries - Amnesty International
sources.claim_summary: Amnesty International report (Jan 2024) 'We Are Facing Extinction': escalating anti-LGBTI sentiment, the weaponization of law and their human-rights implications in select African countries - country profiles including Zambia, documenting the 2022/23 surge in fear, attacks, oppression and hostility.

sources.title: Zambia - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2021 Human Rights Report for Zambia: official assessment - same-sex conduct criminalised under sections 155 and 156 of the Penal Code; societal discrimination; arrests and prosecutions reported.

sources.title: Dignity Debased: Forced Anal Examinations in Homosexuality Prosecutions | HRW
sources.claim_summary: HRW report (July 2016) 'Dignity Debased': forced anal examinations in homosexuality prosecutions - reported in at least eight countries in five years; lack evidentiary value and constitute cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment that may amount to torture; victims described them as painful, degrading, and a form of sexual violence (Zambia among the countries documented).

sources.title: Zambia - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2022 Human Rights Report for Zambia: official assessment - continued criminalisation and societal discrimination.
US State Department 2010 Human Rights Report for Zambia (archived): documents criminalisation and societal discrimination - baseline assessment.
